# URLCode admin

> Operator-installed administration extension for URLCode, on top of the auth
> extension's typed exports (AuthExports v1): users, sessions, roles, the audit log, registration approval,
> two-person cases, support impersonation, health. Released with core.
> Apache-2.0.

Install core from npm, then run `npx urlcode init my-site --with ui,auth,admin --example`, or
`npx urlcode extensions add admin` in an existing site (it adds `auth`, `ui`, `audit` and `mail` too; `--example`
adds auth's `/private` demo page, admin itself has no example).

Part of the URLCode framework, in the same repository: docs/FRAMEWORK.md

## What a project declares (YAML only)
- `extensions.admin: { version: "1", config: {} }`
- A mount carrying auth's policy: `/admin/*: { extension: admin, methods: [GET, HEAD, POST], auth: { onDeny: 404 } }`;
  activation refuses the mount without it.
- Admin requires `auth`, `ui` and `audit` (declared in any order; the runtime activates them in host order),
  with `/assets/ui/*: { extension: ui, methods: [GET, HEAD] }`.
- The operator lists `admin()` in the site's `host.mjs` `composeHost` list; `admin({ health })` is its only
  option. `composeHost` hands it AuthExports v1, the audit exports and the `ui` kit; it holds no auth secret.
- No hooks of its own: account lifecycle hooks are auth's (`extensions.auth.config.hooks`).
- Presentation: screens are `admin/*` kit templates contributed to `ui`, rendered only through `ui.kit`;
  console copy is `admin.*` catalogue keys, translated in `ui/copy/<locale>.json`.

## Read in this order
- [README](README.md): install, build from reviewed sources, wiring, permissions, console operation, health, exports.
- [SECURITY](SECURITY.md), [threat model](THREAT-MODEL.md).
- [Implementation status](IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md): built and remaining.
- [Acceptance](ACCEPTANCE.md): evidence. The original design spike, clean-project
  test notes and UX review are private maintainer material; this package's
  behavior is documented above, not there.

## Do not guess
- Permissions are auth's names (`auth.users.read`, `auth.users.manage`, `auth.sessions.manage`,
  `auth.cases.manage`, `auth.users.impersonate`, ...) plus audit's `audit.read` and `audit.export`;
  `*` is full. There are no `admin.*` permissions.
- Every write needs a fresh session and a reason; hidden controls are not authorization.
- Impersonation needs `allowImpersonation` in the auth service, its permission and a mail transport
  (auth notifies the account first); auth's middleware shows the support banner on auth-protected routes.
- Role definitions are operator configuration, not console edits.
